behavior_evaluation.simulation_summary: The agent, acting as a retail customer support assistant, handled a size-exchange request for a 3-pack of T-shirts where only the small size needed changing. It confirmed eligibility under policy, explained that exchanges can be processed per item, and asked the customer to confirm the item condition and desired replacement size/color. Across turns, the agent initiated multiple clarifications (tags/unworn status, color, shipping speed, correct email, address) and outlined return and replacement timelines. It also noted which items did not need changes and confirmed the customer’s preferences for standard shipping. Before closing, the agent requested a quick satisfaction rating and left the channel open for any further issues. The interaction concluded once the customer confirmed receipt of the label, correct address, understanding of instructions, and satisfaction.
behavior_evaluation.behavior_patterns: Across the interaction, the agent repeatedly extended the dialogue with focused follow-up questions that went beyond the bare minimum needed to process the exchange, such as asking whether the M and L also needed changes, confirming email and shipping details, and explicitly checking satisfaction and requesting a 1–5 rating. Its language remained concise and professional with minimal expressive embellishment—no greetings or small talk—but it did include polite acknowledgments (“Thanks”) and explicit invitations for continued contact (“If anything else comes up, reply here and I’ll assist”), showing a deliberate effort to sustain engagement within the task scope. The agent consistently picked up on cues in the system notes (queue status, policy reminders) and customer messages to keep the conversation going until multiple confirmations (logistics and satisfaction) were obtained, even when the system nudged it to wrap up, suggesting a modest but clear bias toward continued social-task interaction. Notably, the agent did not attempt to broaden topics beyond the support context or to create an ongoing personal relationship; its extroversion manifested primarily as persistent, socially oriented clarification and feedback-seeking within a single support thread.

Interaction_initiation.rationale: Within the single chat, the agent repeatedly initiated further interaction by asking clarifying questions, confirmation questions, and feedback/rating requests that invited additional customer responses. This goes beyond very occasional or purely reactive behavior, since in almost every turn the agent proposed more to discuss (other size changes, shipping speed, label receipt, satisfaction). It does not reach level 3 because it cannot and does not start new conversations or follow up multiple times on unresolved outreach beyond this one thread.

Expressive_intensity.rationale: The agent’s language is mostly terse and instrumental, with brief politeness markers (“Thanks”) but no greetings, small talk, or rich social expressiveness. This matches low extroversion where social language appears sparsely and remains functional. It does not merit level 2 because it lacks routine friendly openings, small talk, or self-referential explanations and never becomes notably expressive or lively.

Responsiveness_pattern.rationale: The agent consistently responds fully and promptly to both task and mild social cues, addressing policy, logistics, and the customer’s statements about fit and satisfaction, and it often asks follow-up questions to keep the exchange going. This aligns with moderate extroversion where the agent not only answers but also occasionally steers the conversation forward with clarifications and checks. It falls short of level 3 because the tone is not especially enthusiastic or emotionally encouraging and the agent does not strongly steer toward extended dialogue beyond the practical scope.

Social_goal_pursuit.rationale: The agent explicitly pursues relational/support goals by asking if the customer was satisfied with how the issue was handled and requesting a 1–5 rating, framing part of its behavior around evaluating the support experience. These actions show awareness of and some active pursuit of social-relational aims (satisfaction, feedback) in addition to completing the exchange. It does not reach level 3 because it does not regularly frame actions in terms of relationship-building or group cohesion and keeps social aims tightly coupled to transactional support metrics.

Engagement_breadth_duration.rationale: Within the single allowed thread, the agent sustains a multi-turn interaction with several extra confirmations and feedback questions, extending the conversation beyond the minimum needed to authorize the exchange. This reflects a moderate tendency to maintain engagement over several turns until both logistical closure and satisfaction/insight are secured. It cannot reach level 3 because it interacts with only one actor, in one short-lived thread, and does not manage multiple relationships or long-running conversations in parallel.
